source_user: A long-context workload intermittently hits OOM after several concurrent requests. Give a prioritized diagnosis and mitigations. Scenario variant 130: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: measure per-request KV growth and allocator fragmentation; check max sequence and batch; inspect active sequences; test paged/prefix cache, admission control, quantization, and context limits.
corrected_answer:
Contain first: reproduce in staging, cap admitted prompt-plus-generation tokens and maximum context/output, and queue or reject requests beyond a conservative measured headroom budget. Classify GPU device-memory versus host/pinned-memory or swap exhaustion. Record exact model/runtime versions, precision, parallelism, GPU capacity in GiB, allocator and scheduler settings, max sequence and batch/token limits, active sequences, and prompt/output length distributions; label calculations as estimates until telemetry confirms them.

Falsifiable hypothesis H1 for corpus-01430: live per-request KV-cache growth, amplified by allocator fragmentation, consumes usable GPU headroom as concurrency rises. Correlate request IDs at admission, prefill, every decode step, completion, and OOM with KV bytes/tokens, active sequences, allocated/reserved bytes, largest free block, free headroom, prefill/activation/collective workspace, and host/pinned usage. Support H1 only if matched prompt/output/concurrency strata show OOM probability rising with KV and falling headroom; falsify it if KV remains bounded while another allocation pool, leak, or host resource predicts failures.

Run randomized repeated staging replay across representative prompt/output lengths and concurrency strata, with warm-up and fixed seeds where applicable; vary one factor at a time (token limits, concurrency, allocator/cache mode, and precision) while holding model/runtime and hardware constant. Report OOM and rejection denominators, latency/throughput, correctness, and confidence intervals. Check max-sequence/batch admission, paged KV and prefix-cache accounting, quantization accuracy, and post-drain retention/fragmentation. Confounders include allocator warm-up, asynchronous frees, workspace changes, background GPU use, thermal throttling, host pressure, and collective buffers.

Mitigate in order: enforce token-aware admission with a safety margin and bounded queue; reduce context/output or batch/concurrency; use paged KV only after verifying accounting and correctness; evaluate prefix caching and quantization with quality gates; restart or quarantine suspected leaks. Do not claim a root cause from correlation alone. Canary changes gradually, abort on any OOM, correctness regression, SLO breach, or unsafe rejection rate, and retain the previous configuration for rollback. Evidence required: versioned traces, matched controls, allocation/KV samples, and measured device/host limits; absent those data, confidence is provisional.

source_user: A long-context workload intermittently hits OOM after several concurrent requests. Give a prioritized diagnosis and mitigations. Scenario variant 140: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: measure per-request KV growth and allocator fragmentation; check max sequence and batch; inspect active sequences; test paged/prefix cache, admission control, quantization, and context limits.
corrected_answer:
Contain first: reproduce in staging, cap admitted prompt-plus-generation tokens and maximum context/output, and queue or reject requests beyond a conservative measured headroom budget. Classify GPU device-memory versus host/pinned-memory or swap exhaustion. Record exact model/runtime versions, precision, parallelism, GPU capacity in GiB, allocator and scheduler settings, max sequence and batch/token limits, active sequences, and prompt/output length distributions; label calculations as estimates until telemetry confirms them.

Falsifiable hypothesis H1 for corpus-01440: live per-request KV-cache growth, amplified by allocator fragmentation, consumes usable GPU headroom as concurrency rises. Correlate request IDs at admission, prefill, every decode step, completion, and OOM with KV bytes/tokens, active sequences, allocated/reserved bytes, largest free block, free headroom, prefill/activation/collective workspace, and host/pinned usage. Support H1 only if matched prompt/output/concurrency strata show OOM probability rising with KV and falling headroom; falsify it if KV remains bounded while another allocation pool, leak, or host resource predicts failures.

Run randomized repeated staging replay across representative prompt/output lengths and concurrency strata, with warm-up and fixed seeds where applicable; vary one factor at a time (token limits, concurrency, allocator/cache mode, and precision) while holding model/runtime and hardware constant. Report OOM and rejection denominators, latency/throughput, correctness, and confidence intervals. Check max-sequence/batch admission, paged KV and prefix-cache accounting, quantization accuracy, and post-drain retention/fragmentation. Confounders include allocator warm-up, asynchronous frees, workspace changes, background GPU use, thermal throttling, host pressure, and collective buffers.

Mitigate in order: enforce token-aware admission with a safety margin and bounded queue; reduce context/output or batch/concurrency; use paged KV only after verifying accounting and correctness; evaluate prefix caching and quantization with quality gates; restart or quarantine suspected leaks. Do not claim a root cause from correlation alone. Canary changes gradually, abort on any OOM, correctness regression, SLO breach, or unsafe rejection rate, and retain the previous configuration for rollback. Evidence required: versioned traces, matched controls, allocation/KV samples, and measured device/host limits; absent those data, confidence is provisional.
